subject: german
title: Clothing Items
welcome_lead: T-shirt, Hose, Schuhe — what you wear.
final_note: Clothes vocab for shopping and describing.

walkthroughs.body_html: Das T-Shirt (neuter), der Pullover (m), die Jacke (f). Mix of genders — learn the article with each word.
Die Hose = trousers (singular in German, plural in English). Die Schuhe = shoes (plural). Das Kleid = dress.
Ich trage = I wear. 'Ich trage eine blaue Jacke' = 'I'm wearing a blue jacket'. Eine (a, feminine) — articles vary.

mcqs.q: Which relative pronoun do you use for 'the man WHOM I saw' in German?
options: It depends on the speaker's mood.

mcqs.q: In 'Heute gehe ich ins Kino', why does 'gehe' come second?
options: Heute is always followed by a verb.
German is a V2 language - the conjugated verb is the second element in main clauses.

mcqs.q: When does 'in' take the accusative vs dative?
options: Accusative for movement INTO a place; dative for location IN a place.
It depends on the speaker's mood.
It always takes the same case.
